key_insight: A selective, tree-anchored combination reduced photovoltaic forecast MAE by 3.21% versus the strongest standalone tree model across 15–240-minute horizons.
engineering_relevance: Solar forecasting pipelines can improve accuracy by combining complementary predictions while assigning zero weight to unhelpful models.
method: Combine LightGBM with seven neural predictors using nonnegative weights that sum to one.
Fit shared cross-horizon weights to MAE, with the tree providing a development-stage fallback.
Test horizon-specific weights, alternative losses and a bounded neural correction.
evidence_signal: On 56,078 windows from two co-located public PVDAQ systems, the historical shared-MAE combination lowered scaled MAE by 3.21%; the latest neural correction added no further MAE improvement.
watch_item: Both analyses reused a previously inspected evaluation period, so independent validation is needed before assuming gains generalize.
paper_title: Reducing Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Forecast Error through Tree-Anchored Expert Combination
